module_title: Advanced Cyber Defense - Encryption Keys, Signatures, and VPNs
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical IT Officer papers, this advanced module breaks down modern cryptographic key systems (Public/Private), network tunneling protocols, and advanced firewall inspection methods.

core_concepts.title: Symmetric Encryption
core_concepts.description: A cryptography method where the **EXACT SAME KEY (Single Key)** is used to both encrypt (lock) and decrypt (unlock) the data. It is very fast but slightly less secure because the sender must share this single secret key with the receiver over the internet.

core_concepts.title: Asymmetric Encryption (Public-Key Cryptography)
core_concepts.description:
A highly secure, modern method that uses a mathematical pair of **TWO DIFFERENT KEYS**:
1. **Public Key**: Shared openly with everyone. It is used strictly to 'Encrypt' (lock) the data.
2. **Private Key**: Kept entirely secret by the owner. It is used strictly to 'Decrypt' (unlock) the data.

core_concepts.title: Digital Signature
core_concepts.description: The electronic equivalent of a physical signature. It is a mathematical scheme used to verify two things: **Authentication** (the message actually came from the claimed sender) and **Data Integrity** (the document was not altered or tampered with during transit).

core_concepts.title: VPN (Virtual Private Network)
core_concepts.description: A technology that creates a secure, 'Encrypted Tunnel' over a less secure public network (like the open Internet). It heavily encrypts your data traffic and masks your IP address, hiding your physical location and online identity from trackers and hackers.

important_entities.name: Stateful Inspection
important_entities.significance: A 3rd-generation firewall technology that doesn't just look at individual data packets blindly. It remembers the 'State' of the active connection and monitors the entire context of the traffic, making it vastly superior to basic packet-filtering firewalls.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will try to trick you into saying 'The Public Key is used to decrypt data'. **Strict Rule:** In Asymmetric encryption, the Public Key CANNOT decrypt anything. Decryption is performed Exclusively and ONLY by the Private Key.

A VPN provides privacy and encrypts your traffic in transit. However, a VPN does NOT protect your computer if you voluntarily download a virus. A VPN cannot scan or kill malware; you still need an Antivirus for that.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember that Asymmetric relies on a pair of two different keys (Public and Private), whereas Symmetric uses only one.

exam_strategy_tips: For Mains exams, deeply understand the function of 'Asymmetric Encryption'. Secure websites (HTTPS) and Banking portals rely heavily on this Public/Private key architecture to securely process your passwords and credit card data.
